mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the prior 3 months of lower rates (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment benefits claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a decline in new job openings (not directly observable here) signals weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >10% from the prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite sustained PAYEMS increases over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) unexpectedly exceeds 3% in the prior month, investors anticipate future rate cuts, which boosts equity valuations and drives a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL exceeds 3% in the prior month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL over-shoots 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% suggests weakening manufacturing demand, which reduces future earnings expectations and produces a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% from prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (Rank IC < 0.05) during the INDPRO contraction month.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (UNRATE) above 4% indicate central bank patience is ending, prompting a preemptive rate hike which depresses equity valuations and yields a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE remains above 4% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the prior month of UNRATE < 4%.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden spike in housing starts (not available in the catalog) would typically signal economic recovery, but here we proxy with a sharp drop in RSAFS (residential construction spending). Such a decline suggests cooling housing demand and a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% from prior month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not lower than the 30-day average prior to the RSAFS drop.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (not directly observable but implied by GDPC1) exceeds 3% in the prior quarter, it indicates robust demand which supports a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when GDPC1 growth is as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in retail sales (not directly observable but proxy via a composite of labor and demand indicators such as PAYEMS and HOUST) suggests softening consumer spending, which predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: Both PAYEMS and HOUST decrease sequentially over two months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not negative when both indicators show improvement.
